title: Settings
subtitle: Manage device name, screenshot shortcut, LAN sync, and version info.

basic.title: Basic
basic.deviceNameHelper: The name other devices see on the local network.
basic.receiveDirHelper: Files received over the local network are saved here.
basic.gamePluginDirHelper: Each subfolder is a game. Default is plugins under the cc-partner data root.

shortcut.title: Shortcuts
shortcut.recordingHelper: Recording keys; Esc cancels, Delete clears.
shortcut.recordingCmdCtrlRejected: Cmd and Ctrl cannot be used together (they collapse to the same modifier). Use Cmd+Shift or keep only one of those keys.

screenshot.label: Screenshot shortcut
screenshot.helper: Select an area and copy it to the clipboard.

experimental.title: Beta features
experimental.subtitle: These features are off by default. Turn one on to show its entry points. Settings for enabled features appear as tabs at the bottom of this page. Turning it off hides the entry immediately and does not delete saved data.

battery.label: Charging mode
battery.helper: Switch charging/unlimited in the sidebar and spend balance on the workbench.

game.label: Game mode
game.helper: Open the game hub and word flashcards from the sidebar, and configure the plugin folder.

browser.label: Web browsing
browser.helper: Preview the project web page on the workbench and on mobile.

automation.label: Project automation
automation.helper: Manage orchestration tasks on the desktop workbench and on mobile.

cloudSync.label: Cloud sync
cloudSync.helper: Sync across networks through a GitHub private repository.

cloudSync.title: Cloud sync
cloudSync.subtitle: Sync across networks via a GitHub private repository. Git access (SSH key or HTTPS credentials) must be configured on this machine.

repoUrl.label: Repository URL
repoUrl.helper: e.g. git@github.com:user/repo.git or an HTTPS URL.

branch.label: Branch (optional)
branch.helper: Leave empty to use the repository default branch.

enabled.label: Enable cloud sync
enabled.helper: Automatically sync Prompts, Prompt history, and Scratchpad. Agent Hub instructions and assets are backed up automatically and require confirmed import in Agent Hub to restore.

auto.label: Auto sync on a schedule
auto.helper: Automatically sync at the configured interval.

interval.label: Sync interval
interval.helper: Interval between automatic syncs, in seconds.

githubTrending.title: AI tools (Claude CLI)
githubTrending.subtitle: Configure the local Claude Code CLI shared by GitHub Trending explanations and Prompt Optimizer. Prompt Optimizer always uses Claude Code; output language follows the current UI language. Trending explanations are cached locally; Prompt Optimizer only shows and copies the current result.

aiEnabled.label: Enable GitHub explanations
aiEnabled.helper: When off, the homepage still shows GitHub descriptions. Prompt Optimizer can still call Claude CLI with this path and model.

claudeCliPath.label: Claude CLI path
claudeCliPath.helper: Used by GitHub explanations and Prompt Optimizer. Use claude, or a full path such as /home/you/.local/bin/claude.

claudeModel.label: Model
claudeModel.helper: Claude Code CLI model alias or full model name for GitHub explanations and Prompt Optimizer. Defaults to sonnet.

cacheTtlHours.label: Cache TTL (hours)
cacheTtlHours.helper: Defaults to 24 hours. Only GitHub Trending fetches and explanations use this cache; Prompt Optimizer is not cached.

githubTrending.applyFailed: Failed to apply Claude CLI config

internalClaude.title: Internal Claude provider
internalClaude.subtitle: Pick a cc-switch Claude provider for cc-partner's own silent calls (commit messages, merge resolution, Prompt optimizer, GitHub explanations, verifier). This does not modify your OS-default ~/.claude/settings.json, so your interactive Claude sessions are unaffected.

provider.label: Provider for internal calls
provider.helper: Only the listed cc-switch Claude providers are shown. Choose 'OS default' to fall back to your normal Claude config.
provider.missingNotice: The previously selected provider no longer exists in cc-switch. Internal calls fall back to the OS default until you pick another.

internalClaude.loadFailed: Failed to load internal Claude provider config: {{error}}
internalClaude.saveFailed: Failed to update internal Claude provider: {{error}}

hotkey.label: Prompt optimizer shortcut
hotkey.helper: Opens the Prompt optimizer overlay in a Workbench terminal. Defaults to tapping Control. It triggers only when Control is pressed and released by itself, so terminal chords such as Control+C still pass through.

hotkey.label: Favorites quick input shortcut
hotkey.helper: Press this shortcut inside a Workbench terminal to open the favorite prompts list; selecting one inserts it into the active session input line without submitting.

promptQuickInputSettings.applyFailed: Failed to apply favorites quick input settings

automation.title: Automation
automation.description: Configure Orchestrator automatic task pickup, verification commands, and full-auto delivery. These settings are saved as this device's global policy.
automation.enabledHint: Allow the Orchestrator scheduler to automatically claim and run queued tasks.
automation.maxConcurrentTasksHint: Maximum automation tasks this device may run at the same time. Range: 1-8.
automation.verificationCommandsHint: One command per line. The backend cleans empty lines and validates length when saved.
automation.deliveryDescription: Control automatic commit, push, and merge steps after verification passes.
automation.autoCommitHint: After verification passes, generate a commit and commit changes in the task worktree.
automation.autoPushTaskBranchHint: Push the task branch to the remote repository after committing.
automation.autoMergeToMainHint: Merge the verified task branch back into the main workspace.
automation.autoPushMainHint: Push the main branch after the main workspace merge completes.
automation.notificationsDescription: Toggle operational notifications by state. Notifications only alert and never run Deliver/Retry actions; bodies never include task titles or project names.
automation.notifyHumanReview: Notify when a task needs review
automation.notifyHumanReviewHint: Send a system notification when a task enters human review (on by default).
automation.notifyBlocked: Notify when a task is blocked
automation.notifyBlockedHint: Send a system notification when a task becomes blocked (on by default).
automation.notifyRemoteOutboxFailedHint: Send a system notification when a remote task outbox delivery fails (on by default).
automation.notifyTaskDone: Notify when a task is done
automation.notifyTaskDoneHint: Send a system notification when a task completes (off by default).
automation.agentAdaptersHint: Owner-local adapter availability (no executable path or credentials).

health.title: Health reminder
health.subtitle: Tune health monitoring work/break thresholds, water interval, quiet hours, and system notifications.

activity.title: Activity stats
activity.subtitle: Tune window-title recording and activity detail retention. These settings affect stats only, not reminder timing.

mobileAccess.title: Mobile Workbench
mobileAccess.description: Open this Workbench from a phone browser on the same local network.
mobileAccess.warning: Any device on the same reachable network can read, write, and execute; the system does not verify caller identity. Mobile can operate terminal input, file edits, and Git.
mobileAccess.empty: No local network URL is available for mobile access.
mobileAccess.copyUnavailable: Clipboard access is unavailable here. Select and copy the link manually.

lanFirewall.title: LAN firewall
lanFirewall.subtitle: Project remote access ports
lanFirewall.description: When another LAN device opens local Workbench projects on this machine, the current P2P HTTP TCP port must allow inbound traffic, and mDNS UDP 5353 must remain available for discovery.
lanFirewall.riskNotice: Any device on the same reachable network can read, write, and execute; the system does not verify caller identity. The listener remains wildcard 0.0.0.0; use the actual TCP port and UDP 5353.
lanFirewall.manualNotice: The app reads firewall state available on this device and shows Open or Closed directly. If the system rules cannot be read, the port is treated as closed and the steps below remain available.
lanFirewall.loadFailed: Failed to check LAN firewall dependency
lanFirewall.copyFailed: Failed to copy command. Select and copy it manually.

macos.summary: On macOS, prefer allowing cc-partner in the application firewall. The relevant network requirements are the current TCP port and UDP 5353.
macos.stepSystemSettings: Open System Settings → Network → Firewall → Options.
macos.stepAllowApp: Allow cc-partner to receive incoming connections. If it is missing, use the command below to add the current app to the application firewall.
macos.stepPorts: Confirm your network policy allows the current TCP port and UDP 5353. The app will not run sudo automatically.
macos.allowAppCommand: Add the current app to the application firewall
macos.unblockAppCommand: Allow inbound connections for the current app

windows.summary: On Windows, use Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security or add inbound rules from an elevated terminal.
windows.stepAdmin: Open PowerShell or Command Prompt as Administrator.
windows.stepRules: Add two inbound allow rules: the current TCP port and UDP 5353.
windows.tcpCommand: Allow the current P2P TCP port

linux.summary: Linux/Ubuntu commonly uses ufw or firewalld. Choose the command set matching the firewall enabled on your distribution.
linux.stepChooseFirewall: Check whether this system uses ufw or firewalld.
linux.stepReload: firewalld permanent rules require reload; ufw writes the rule immediately.
linux.ufwTcp: ufw allow current P2P TCP port
linux.firewalldTcp: firewalld allow current P2P TCP port

unsupported.summary: No command template is available for this platform. Manually allow inbound TCP on the current port and UDP 5353 in the system firewall.
unsupported.stepManual: Add inbound rules manually: the current TCP port is used for project access, and UDP 5353 is used for mDNS discovery.

backup.title: Export / Restore
backup.subtitle: Export a verifiable backup archive, or restore selected domains from one. A pre-restore backup is created automatically before restore.
backup.modeReplaceHelper: Clear selected domains first, then import
backup.confirmRestoreText: Selected domains will be restored with the chosen mode. This writes local data.
backup.confirmRollbackText: This job will be rolled back using its pre-restore backup.

agentLedger.title: Agent usage stats
agentLedger.helper: Clear locally recorded Agent usage stats (session counts, duration, tokens/cost, etc.). View them from the Workbench header button “Agent usage stats”. Does not delete terminal sessions, automation tasks, prompts, conversation content, or sync data.
agentLedger.clearConfirmBody: Deletes all local Agent usage stats permanently. Terminal sessions, automation tasks, prompts, and conversation content are unchanged.

onboardingReset.title: First-launch onboarding
onboardingReset.helper: Clear LAN risk disclosure acknowledgement and permission onboarding marker so the next launch repeats the first-run flow. Prompt, scratchpad, and Claude Code content are kept.
onboardingReset.confirmBody: This clears LAN risk disclosure acknowledgement and the permission onboarding marker, stops the local backend service, and quits the app. Prompt, scratchpad, Claude Code content, and device settings are not deleted. macOS privacy permissions (Screen Recording, etc.) cannot be revoked by the app — turn them off in System Settings → Privacy & Security if needed. After confirmation the app exits; reopen it to see the first-run guides.
